methodology.metric: assembled function-body bytes, including prologue/epilogue; external helper bodies excluded

methodology.integer_division: Rust unchecked intrinsics match the C valid-input domain; no Rust panic guards
methodology.signed_c_arithmetic: unsigned intermediates and casts; two-complement conversion and arithmetic right shift required
methodology.float_widths: C sizeof assertions prevent double/long double silently becoming f32
methodology.instruction_counts: source mnemonics only; inline db machine code reported separately
methodology.scope: static codegen comparison; no cycle estimates or target runtime equivalence checks
methodology.library_cost: SDCC archive dependency bytes for all supported cases; isolated linked reachable ROM sections for Rust string cases; no startup, entry harness or alignment padding

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1097 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 171 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 140 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.
